changes.summary: give the nurse scoped batch-audit instructions
changes.body:
Hive's nurse now uses gpt-6.1-sol with high reasoning. Automatic audit briefs
authorize provisional health records and bounded read-only investigations,
require exact report coverage and verified delivery, and preserve examined
code, claims and request outcomes. Manual health advice remains advice unless
its assignment explicitly grants curation or investigation scope.

Required for automatic audits: deploy the updated nurse role and Colony
runtime together. New requests capture the current role; existing captured
recipes remain unchanged. Use `bee kinds nurse --verbose` to inspect defaults
and the Colony guide for activation. No action is required for manual advice.

changes.summary: guide workflow drivers through focused brief reads
changes.body:
Managed workflow drivers read the full native run brief on entry and each
active task brief once per visit. They refresh briefs when relevant scope,
state or authority changes and use compact Busy Bee views between reads.
This keeps caller completion instructions and stage authority explicit.

Optional: align custom driver prompts with this reading procedure and use
`busybee show --help` to discover frozen instruction expansion.

`bee retry REQUEST --resume-cancelled` permits deliberate replacement of a
cancelled request with unfinished work and no existing replacement. It retains
the workflow assignment, captures current kind defaults and explicit overrides,
and creates a fresh identity bound to the submitting host. Human/HITL
reservations, conflicting open requests and existing task claims retain their
normal treatment. Acknowledged failures remain ineligible.

The old request retains its cancellation, closure time and identity. `bee status`
exposes replacement IDs while the old disposition stays cancelled/resolved and
outside failure attention. Interrupted publication retains confirmed IDs;
repeating a superseded request repairs query labels and refuses a duplicate.

Optional: after verifying the old execution has stopped and deciding to resume
its assignment, read `bee retry --help` and invoke the explicit option with any
needed recipe overrides. Request closure alone is not process verification.

Required when adopting this recovery path: install Bee and Busy Bee from the
same updated Hive revision. Keep Bee's Colony CLI, runtime, worker and watchdog
companions together. Coordinate active work before deliberately restarting an
upgraded daemon; follow `colony daemon restart --help` with its retained selection.

changes.summary: group workflow and observer protocols under system
changes.body:
Busy Bee stage dispatch uses `bee system dispatch-stage`. Colony's auxiliary
observers submit through `bee system assess` and `bee system report`. The former
top-level paths are removed. Ordinary workers continue to use `bee finish`.

Required: upgrade Bee, Busy Bee and Colony together. Update custom integration
calls and observer prompts to the system paths; use `bee system --help` for the
protocols and their callers.

changes.summary: add an operational Architect to Hive's bee catalogue
changes.body:
Hive's repository configuration adds a read-only Pi/Astra-high Architect
for feature continuity review and task unblocking. Detailed code/test review
remains Reviewer's role; Librarian retains architectural memory.

Optional: adopt the repository kind and specialist protocol with a compatible
Pi formula. Installing Bee alone does not copy repository kind configuration.

The `bee list` command has been removed.

Required: update `bee list` callers to use focused native Beads queries for
request discovery, then use exact request IDs with `bee status`, `bee result`
or `bee stop`. Read each command's focused `--help` before use.

changes.summary: clarify workflow result notes for stage completion
changes.body: `bee response --help` identifies workflow notes as Busy Bee's original `{choice,data}` outcome, covering both `complete` and `record-result`. No adoption action is required.

changes.summary: expose delegation history separately from Colony
changes.body:
Use `bee changelog` to read Bee's bundled release records without submitting
work or accessing a tracker. Bee and Colony retain separate tool histories
even though they share a package.

changes.summary: Managed bees retain configured harness paths under native daemon supervision, including the location of existing Codex authentication.
